newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY TOP VOTE-GETTER ON A.L. ALL-STAR TEAM.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY TOP VOTE-GETTER ON A.L. ALL-STAR TEAM.

text.p: Seattle Mariners outfielder Ken Griffey Jr has earned his eighth consecutive American League All-Star berth and was the top vote-getter for the third time, the league announced Monday.

Griffey, who is on pace to break Roger Maris's single-season record of 61 home runs, received 3,514,340 votes in balloting by the fans for the All-Star Game, to be played July 8 at Jacobs Field in Cleveland.

For a change, it appears Griffey will actually play in the mid-summer classic. He missed the last two with injuries, but is among three members of the Mariners elected as starters, joining shortstop Alex Rodriguez and designated hitter Edgar Martinez.

Also placing three starters were the Baltimore Orioles. Cal Ripken Jr won at third base after being named at shortstop 14 times. It will be his 13th appearance as a starter. Second baseman Roberto Alomar and outfielder Brady Anderson also were voted to the starting lineup.
The final three spots went to Texas Rangers catcher Ivan Rodriguez, New York Yankees first baseman Tino Martinez and Cleveland Indians outfielder David Justice.
The closest race was at first base, where Martinez edged the Cleveland Indians' Jim Thome by just over 19,000 votes. Martinez finished with 866,722 votes, the lowest winning number at any position.
Rodriguez earned 1,666,384 votes, over 100,000 more than Cleveland's Sandy Alomar.

Ripken finished second in the A.L. balloting with 2,571,985 votes, more than doubling his nearest competitor at third base, Matt Williams of Cleveland. Rodriguez had 1,854,758 votes and Roberto Alomar got 1,657,418.
Edgar Martinez finished with 1,213,429 votes, while in the outfield, Justice received 1,840,716 votes and Anderson 1,197,617.
The National League starters will be announced Tuesday and the pitchers and reserves for both leagues will be released Wednesday.
